sanskrit: yat prācīnaṃ barhi stṛṇāti yajñāya ca devebhyaś cā vṛścate ||
english: When one strews the barhis eastward, it is cut off for the sacrifice and for the gods.

sanskrit: yad dakṣiṇācīnaṃ barhi stṛṇāti yamāya ca pitṛbhyaś cā vṛścate ||
english: When one strews the barhis southward, it is cut off for Yama and for the Pitṛs.

sanskrit: yat pratīcīnaṃ barhi stṛṇāty akṛtapūrvaṃ karoti ||
english: When one strews the barhis westward, one does what has never been done before.

sanskrit: yad udīcīnaṃ barhi stṛṇāti somāya ca rājñe saptaṛṣibhyaś cā vṛścate ||
english: When one strews the barhis northward, it is cut off for King Soma and for the Seven Sages.

sanskrit: yat purastāt pātrasya tsaruṃ karoty arśaḥ pratigrahītur mukhe jāyate ||
english: When one fashions the handle of the vessel in front, hemorrhoids arise in the mouth of the recipient.

sanskrit: yad dakṣiṇataḥ pātrasya tsaruṃ karoti yamāya ca pitṛbhyaś cā vṛścate ||
english: When one fashions the handle of the vessel on the south side, it is cut off for Yama and for the Pitṛs.

sanskrit: yat paścāt pātrasya tsaruṃ karoti pratīcī pratigrahītāraṃ śaravya rcchati ||
english: When one fashions the handle of the vessel behind, a westward-flying arrow strikes the recipient.

sanskrit: yad uttarataḥ pātrasya tsaruṃ karoti somāya ca rājñe saptaṛṣibhyaś cā vṛścate ||
english: When one fashions the handle of the vessel on the north side, it is cut off for King Soma and for the Seven Sages.

sanskrit: yac chukro bhavaty ādityānām eva priyaṃ dhāmopaiti | sa yaḥ śukraṃ prāśnīyād ādityānāṃ tvā priyeṇa dhāmnā prāśnāmīty enaṃ prāśnīyāt | tataś cainam anyena dhāmnā prāśnāty ādityebhyaś cā vṛścate ||
english: When it is bright, it attains the dear abode of the Ādityas. He who would eat of the bright one should eat it saying: 'I eat thee with the dear abode of the Ādityas.' Thereupon he eats it with another abode; and it is cut off for the Ādityas.

sanskrit: yat phalīkṛto bhavati viśveṣām eva devānāṃ priyaṃ (…) | sa yaḥ phalīkṛtaṃ prāśnīyād viśveṣāṃ tvā devānāṃ priyeṇa dhāmnā (…) | (…) prāśnāti viśvebhyo devebhyaś cā vṛścate ||
english: When it is husked, it is the dear (abode) of the Viśve Devās. He who would eat of the husked one should (eat it saying): 'I eat thee with the dear abode of all the gods'; (he eats it thus). It is cut off for the Viśve Devās.

sanskrit: yad aphalīkṛto bhavati marutām eva priyaṃ (…) | sa yo 'phalīkṛtaṃ prāśnīyān marutāṃ tvā priyeṇa (…) | (…) prāśnāti marudbhyaś cā vṛścate ||
english: When it is unhusked, it is the dear (abode) of the Maruts. He who would eat of the unhusked one should (eat it saying): 'I eat thee with the dear (abode) of the Maruts'; (he eats it thus). It is cut off for the Maruts.

sanskrit: yad avakṣāmo bhavaty agner eva (…) | sa yo 'vakṣāmaṃ prāśnīyād agnes tvā priyeṇa (…) | (…) prāśnāty agnaye cā vṛścate ||
english: When it is shrunken, it is (the dear abode) of Agni alone. He who would eat of the shrunken one should (eat it saying): 'I eat thee with the dear (abode) of Agni'; (he eats it thus). It is cut off for Agni.

sanskrit: yad anavakṣāmo bhavati mitrāvaruṇayor eva (…) | sa yo 'navakṣāmaṃ prāśnīyān mitrāvaruṇayos tvā priyeṇa (…) | (…) prāśnāti mitrāvaruṇābhyāṃ cā vṛścate ||
english: When it is unshrunken, it is (the dear abode) of Mitra and Varuṇa. He who would eat of the unshrunken one should (eat it saying): 'I eat thee with the dear (abode) of Mitra and Varuṇa'; (he eats it thus). It is cut off for Mitra and Varuṇa.

sanskrit: yad aklinno bhavati- -indrasyaiva (…) | sa yo 'klinnaṃ prāśnīyād indrasya tvā (…) | (…) prāśnāti- -indrāya cā vṛścate ||
english: When it is dry, it is (the dear abode) of Indra alone. He who would eat of the dry one should (eat it saying): 'I eat thee (with the dear abode) of Indra'; (he eats it thus). It is cut off for Indra.

sanskrit: yat klinno bhavati pitṝṇām eva (…) | sa yaḥ klinnaṃ prāśnīyāt pitṝṇāṃ tvā (…) | (…) prāśnāti pitṛbhyaś cā vṛścate ||
english: When it is moist, it is (the dear abode) of the Pitṛs alone. He who would eat of the moist one should (eat it saying): 'I eat thee (with the dear abode) of the Pitṛs'; (he eats it thus). It is cut off for the Pitṛs.

sanskrit: yat kṣudro bhavaty apām eva (…) | sa yaḥ kṣudraṃ prāśnīyād apāṃ tvā priyeṇa (…) | (…) prāśnāty adbhyaś cā vṛścate ||
english: When it is small, it is (the dear abode) of the Waters alone. He who would eat of the small one should (eat it saying): 'I eat thee with the dear (abode) of the waters'; (he eats it thus). It is cut off for the Waters.

sanskrit: yac chithiro bhavati diśām eva (…) | sa yaḥ śithiraṃ prāśnīyād diśāṃ tvā (…) | [see 1d (…) prāśnāti digbhyaś cā vṛścate ||
english: When it is loose, it is (the dear abode) of the Directions alone. He who would eat of the loose one should (eat it saying): 'I eat thee (with the dear abode) of the Directions'; (he eats it thus). It is cut off for the Directions.

sanskrit: yad gulantī bhavati prajāpater eva (…) | sa yo gulantinaṃ prāśnīyāt prajāpateṣ ṭvā (…) | (…) prāśnāti prajāpataye cā vṛścate ||
english: When it is a gulantī grain, it is (the dear abode) of Prajāpati alone. He who would eat of the gulantī grain should (eat it saying): 'I eat thee (with the dear abode) of Prajāpati'; (he eats it thus). It is cut off for Prajāpati.

sanskrit: yac chuṣko bhavaty ūrdhvanabhasa eva priyaṃ dhāmopaiti | sa yaḥ śuṣkaṃ prāśnīyād ūrdhvanabhasas tvā priyeṇa dhāmnā prāśnāmīty enaṃ prāśnīyāt | tataś cainam anyena dhāmnā prāśnāty ūrdhvanabhase cā vṛścate ||
english: When it is withered, it attains the dear abode of the Uppermost Sky. He who would eat of the withered one should eat it saying: 'I eat thee with the dear abode of the Uppermost Sky.' Thereupon he eats it with another abode; and it is cut off for the Uppermost Sky.
